_about: Example approval policy for echo-agent. Copy this file to data/permissions.json (which is gitignored) and edit there. Rules are evaluated in order — first match wins. Unknown fields like _about / _comment_* are ignored by load_policy.
_docs: https://github.com/dengdenghua/echo-os  ·  see docs/permissions.md for the full guide.

rules._comment_section: ── Browser reads (headless Playwright) · enable fetch + scrape paths ──
rules._comment_note: Comment these out if you don't want agents to drive Chromium. The url_guard layer still blocks SSRF / private-network targets even when allowed here.

rules._comment_section: ── Browser writes / interaction · default DENY · uncomment per skill if you want them ──
rules._comment_note: browser_click, browser_type, browser_screenshot, live_browser_* skills stay gated. The live_browser_* family in particular operates your real, logged-in browser tab via the Electron desktop bridge — leaving it gated is the whole point of Patch 2.
rules.reason: user-confirm: live bridge drives your real browser

rules._comment_section: ── Web egress · fetch_url is allowed; webhooks/email/slack stay gated ──
rules.reason: trusted: read-only HTTP GET (url_guard enforces SSRF rules)
trusted: bounded crawler with url_guard, robots checks, and JSONL output

rules._comment_section: ── Shell · narrow allow for safe read-only invocations, hard deny on destructive ──
rules._comment_note: args_contains is a substring check, not a regex. The deny rule fires before the allow because order matters.

rules._comment_section: ── Filesystem writes · default DENY (every write hits the UI) ──
rules._comment_note: If you want a workspace-scoped allow, add an args_contains rule that pins the path prefix. The agent's _SCOPED_ARTIFACT_WRITE_TOOLS shortcut in react_loop already auto-approves writes inside the artifact sandbox; this rule is for everything else.

rules._comment_section: ── Git side-effects · default DENY for anything that mutates remote/branch state ──

rules._comment_note: Even if Capabilities → desktop_automation is ON, keep these gated per-call. Screen capture is a data-egress vector (whatever's on screen leaves the host the moment the screenshot lands in a tool observation).

rules.reason: trusted: status + sandboxed screenshot path (not the bytes)
trusted: queues a token, does not execute
user-confirm: ships screenshot to vision model (egress)
